name: publicWeb_endDirectMessage
description: Web member's door to HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage (direct messages, E9.F1.S7/S18/S19): unfriend — marks the caller's HC.HasherFriendMap row for the thread Removed = 1. A thin wrapper that EXECs the app SP with the same arguments and returns its rowsets unchanged; it adds nothing that could drift from the app. Auth: the wrapped SP's HC6.ValidateAppAuth — token signed for hcapp_endDirectMessage.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The browser's HC.Device id (the web member session). No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token signed for hcapp_endDirectMessage (the SP that validates it). No SQL default.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The direct-message thread to end. Passed straight through.

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth 1232 / 1332 / 1232 signed out) returns the error detail ALONE.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage: On success { success = 1, errorMessage = NULL }; on a refusal after auth { success = 0, errorCode, errorType } then the detail at index 1.

columns.name: errorMessage
columns.description: NULL on success; absent on failure, where the row carries errorCode / errorType instead: 2006 no such conversation (2), 2007 unhandled (5).

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage: After a { success = 0 } envelope: 2006 or 2007.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage with the same arguments — every side effect is the wrapped SP's:
UPDATE HC.HasherFriendMap SET Removed = 1, updatedAt = SYSDATETIMEOFFSET() WHERE UserId = @userId AND ThreadId = @threadId (autocommit — no explicit transaction).
INSERT LOG.GeneralLog ('HC6.hcapp_endDirectMessage', 'Direct message ended', userId, thread) — a separate autocommit statement.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 2006 and in the CATCH (2007).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('<web>', userId NULL, deviceId) then THROW in the wrapper's CATCH, for an error the wrapped SP does not handle itself.

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId and @accessToken have no SQL default (line 16). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
